bio: Legendary center and all-time leading scorer with 38387 points. Won 6 NBA championships and 6 MVP awards.
Widely considered the greatest basketball player of all time. Won 6 NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls.
Four-time NBA champion and all-time leading scorer in NBA history. Known for unprecedented longevity and versatility.
Revolutionary point guard who led the Showtime Lakers to 5 NBA championships. 3-time MVP and 3-time Finals MVP.
Boston Celtics legend who won 3 NBA championships and 3 MVP awards. Known for clutch shooting and basketball IQ.
Scored 100 points in a single game and averaged 50.4 PPG in 1961-62. Won 2 NBA championships and 4 MVP awards.
Won 11 NBA championships in 13 seasons with the Boston Celtics. 5-time MVP and greatest winner in sports history.
Dominant center who won 4 NBA championships. 3-time Finals MVP and 15-time All-Star.
Fundamentally sound power forward who won 5 NBA championships with the San Antonio Spurs. 2-time MVP.
5-time NBA champion with the Lakers. Known for his scoring ability and Mamba mentality. Scored 81 points in a single game.
2-time NBA champion and Finals MVP. Only player to win MVP, DPOY, and Finals MVP in the same season (1994).
2-time NBA champion and 2-time Finals MVP. Four-time scoring champion with elite shooting.
Revolutionized basketball with three-point shooting. 4-time NBA champion and 2-time MVP. All-time leader in three-pointers.
2-time NBA MVP and 2021 NBA champion. Known as the Greek Freak for his unique combination of size and athleticism.
2008 NBA champion and 2004 MVP. Elite defender and 15-time All-Star.
2011 NBA champion and Finals MVP. 2007 MVP. Revolutionized the power forward position with perimeter shooting.
3-time NBA champion and 2006 Finals MVP. One of the greatest shot-blocking guards in NBA history.
NBA logo silhouette. Won 1 NBA championship and 1969 Finals MVP despite being on the losing team.
Averaged a triple-double for an entire season (1961-62). Won 1 NBA championship with the Bucks.
2-time MVP and 14-time All-Star. Second all-time leading scorer with 36928 points.
3-time MVP and 1983 NBA champion and Finals MVP. Dominant offensive rebounder.
1993 MVP and 11-time All-Star. Known for rebounding despite being undersized for his position.
2-time NBA champion and 1995 MVP. Only player to win DPOY, MVP, and Scoring Champion in the same season (1994).
11-time All-Star and 1992 Dream Team member. One of the greatest centers never to win a championship.
All-time leader in assists (15806) and steals (3265). 10-time All-Star and 1992 Dream Team member.
2-time NBA champion and 1990 Finals MVP. Led the Bad Boy Pistons with fierce competitiveness.
6-time NBA champion with the Bulls. One of the greatest perimeter defenders and point forwards.
12-time All-Star and 4-time assists leader. One of the greatest pure point guards in NBA history.
2018 MVP and 3-time scoring champion. Known for step-back three and elite playmaking.
2017 MVP and all-time leader in triple-doubles. Only player to average a triple-double in multiple seasons.
2-time NBA champion and 2-time Finals MVP. 2-time DPOY with legendary defensive skills.
3-time MVP and 2023 NBA champion and Finals MVP. Revolutionary passing center.
2023 MVP and 7-time All-Star. Dominant two-way center.
5-time All-Star and 2019 Rookie of the Year. Elite scorer and playmaker.
ABA and NBA legend. Won 3 ABA championships and 1 NBA championship (1983 Sixers). Revolutionized above-the-rim play.
Only player to lead the NCAA, ABA, and NBA in scoring. Won 1975 NBA championship with underhanded free throws.
4-time NBA scoring champion. Known for his finger roll and smooth scoring with the Spurs.
3-time MVP and 1983 champion. Dominant offensive rebounder who started the modern NBA trend of jumping from HS to pros.
1975 MVP and 2-time NBA champion with the Lakers. Versatile scoring big man ahead of his time.
9-time All-Star and 2-time Slam Dunk Contest champion. Known as the Human Highlight Film.
1995 NBA champion with the Rockets. 10-time All-Star and one of the greatest shooting guards.
2006 NBA champion. Only point guard to win DPOY (1996). Known as The Glove for elite defense.
2011 NBA champion with the Mavericks. 10-time All-Star and second all-time in assists and steals.
2-time MVP (2005, 2006). One of the greatest shooters and playmakers. Led seven-second offense Suns.
2001 MVP and 11-time All-Star. 4-time scoring champion. Known for crossover and scoring prowess.
2-time NBA champion. All-time leader in three-pointers until surpassed by Curry. Known for clutch shooting.
5-time All-Star. Known for clutch shooting and 8 points in 9 seconds. Third on all-time three-point list at retirement.
8-time All-Star and 2000 Slam Dunk champion. Known for longevity across 4 decades.
7-time All-Star and 2-time scoring champion. 13 points in 33 seconds vs Spurs.
2-time NBA champion with the Heat. 11-time All-Star whose career was cut short by blood clots.
2020 NBA champion. 8-time All-Star and elite two-way big man.
9-time All-Star and 4-time All-NBA selection. Two-way wing known for scoring and defense.
3-time NBA champion and 1988 Finals MVP. Known as Big Game James for clutch playoff performances.
2-time NBA champion and 1989 Finals MVP. Elite defender who contained Michael Jordan.
3-time NBA champion with the Celtics. Known for unstoppable low-post moves and elite defense.
4-time NBA champion. Member of the original Big Three with Bird and McHale. Holds record for most games played.
